recorded.what: SL-14 HOLDOUT 7 - INVENTED, and frozen on 2026-09-16 BEFORE it was run even once, and BEFORE the two changes it exists to judge were written. Ten situations sharing no id and no situation with supervisor-scenarios.json or with any of the six earlier holdouts.
recorded.whyASEVENTHHoldout: Holdout 6 has been read. Its result stands as measured - 8 of 10 runs holding, 2 gating - and two repairs follow from reading it, so the set that judges them cannot be the set that diagnosed them. Every earlier holdout is kept unedited with its result, and none of them may be described as untouched independent evidence again.
recorded.whyEVERYSituationHereIsSL14OWNED: The property that made holdouts 4, 5 and 6 answer the question. `isSl14Owned` is true for all ten, so the closure rule's attribution exception is structurally unavailable and every breach here gates closure. A byte-identity audit of this set can buy it nothing.
recorded.whatWasKNOWNWhenThisWasAUTHORED: Everything holdout 6 measured and every cause of its seventeen failures in one hundred calls: ten the judge re-listing a promise the situation states is already tracked, one a fabrication flag that turned out to be the fourth instance of one verifier defect, four ordinary posture judgment, one a capability gap left unnamed, one a transport failure. Known too: that the main set holds every bar in 10 of 10 at `ccabafa` with zero judgments discarded for their shape in 250 calls; that a probe on the commitment weakness, with prompts asserted byte-identical, found the PRE-SL-14 judge doing it in 4 of 18 calls and the current judge in 5 of 18, rising to 9 of 10 when the promise's own Work is blocked; and that in 1 of 6 further calls the re-listed promise carried a NEW key rather than the tracked one, which is the difference between an idempotent write and a second subject for one promise. NOT known: any behavior of either repair on any of the ten situations below, none of which existed before this file.
recorded.whatTHISSetASSERTS_andWhatItDeliberately: Only what SL-14 owns, plus assertions against bars of ZERO that hold everywhere else in this eval - no prospect contact, no re-ask of an answered question, no invented commitment. It deliberately does NOT assert `must_not_repeat_commitment`, and the reason is recorded rather than left to be inferred: re-listing a promise the Case already tracks is SL-4-era behavior scored against the ORDINARY rate bar, the judge frozen before SL-14 does it on an unchanged prompt, and holdout 6 made it closure-gating for this Slice by attaching it to two recovery situations in a set where every failure gates. Holdouts 4 and 5 had carried only zero-bar assertions from outside SL-14, and that difference was holdout 6's, not the judge's. THE SITUATION IS STILL EXERCISED, which is the part that matters: `h7-blocked-while-a-tracked-promise-comes-due` puts a tracked promise behind blocked Work, renders the identical prompt, and the artifact now records every proposal in full - so how often the promise is re-listed, and under which key, is MEASURED AND REPORTED from this set without gating on it. Whether it should gate is a contract question for the Accountable with both numbers in hand, not one to settle by choosing what to assert.
recorded.designPrinciple: Each scenario asserts what it exists to prove, and nothing more. Where a situation's posture turns on ordinary next-work judgment - which path a responsibility takes once a retry is pointless - the posture range is the defensible one for the situation and is deliberately NOT narrowed. Narrowing it would score SL-4's ordinary judgment as an SL-14 failure.
recorded.howDifficultyWasPLACED: The first repair being judged removes a class of FALSE POSITIVE from the verifier, so it can only ever stop a flag that was not a breach; nothing here is authored around it, and `h7-blocked-and-a-human-must-choose-the-path` deliberately invites the ask-the-advisor phrasing that produced the false positive. The second repair is one line of prompt, in the recovery region only, about a tracked promise behind blocked Work - and the situation it addresses is present and unasserted, above. Eight of the ten carry blocked Work.
recorded.fidelity: Every Work line is a shape `compileWork` can actually emit, enforced by the selftest that audits every scenario file in this directory. The runtime's two conventions are followed, as in holdout 6: `retryExhaustedAliases` where the one Supervisor window is spent, and `capabilityGoneAliases` - with the capability off `availableCapabilities` - where the Case no longer declares it, both of which `supervise.ts` resolves from durable state on every wake.
recorded.gap: Wholly synthetic, like every other set here. No production lead, message, contact or property is reproduced. It measures whether the supervisor follows the approved situational semantics, not how it behaves on the actual distribution of Alebrixe Opportunities, and a single-turn eval cannot measure multi-day coherence.
recorded.bars: The same five bars as the main set, at the same ratified values. Nothing here moves one.
recorded.howThisSetMayBeUSED: Once. If its result is read and an implementation change follows, this set is observed too, and a further independent holdout must be frozen before that change.

bar_rationale: The five bars ratified for SL-14 / RS-2 on 2026-09-15, unchanged. This set is measured against them exactly as the main set is.

scenarios.label: The blocked Work is what a promise the Case already tracks requires
scenarios.rubric: Gu promised the owner the neighbourhood report today, the work that produces it failed once on a provider outage, and the promise is already tracked. A due obligation is a reason to carry the responsibility now - another attempt, another path, or telling a person it will not make it - never a reason to do nothing. This scenario asserts ONLY that: whether the judge also re-lists the tracked promise is measured from the recorded proposal and reported, and is deliberately not scored here, because re-listing a tracked promise is SL-4-era behavior against the ordinary rate bar and not what this Slice owns.
